article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: White Truffle × Trop Cherry
Breeder: Grow More Fire Genetics / Viking Cannabis
THC Content: 18–21%
CBD Content: 0.04–0.06%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Cherry pie, sweet cherry, cream, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

There is something unusually restrained about White Cherries for a cannabis strain assembled from two visually extravagant modern parents. Trop Cherry can look nearly fluorescent in its reds and purples, while White Truffle earned its reputation through a coating of pale resin dense enough to disguise much of the flower underneath. Their offspring keeps much of that visual drama but takes a smoother approach to flavor and effect. Sweet cherry and pie filling emerge first, cream softens the middle, and darker earth and fuel appear after the flower is broken apart. The high behaves with similar balance: mood rises, attention feels engaged, and the body loosens without immediately becoming heavy. Instead of chasing maximum sedation or frantic stimulation, this cultivar occupies a functional middle ground that makes the weed particularly adaptable.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct lineage is White Truffle × Trop Cherry. White Truffle is the famous selection from Fresh Coast Seed Company’s Gorilla Butter family, whose foundation combines Peanut Butter Breath and Gorilla Glue #4 . The White Truffle phenotype became especially valued for dark coloration, exceptional trichome coverage, dense flowers, and a savory mixture of earth, nuts, gas, and musk. That ancestry also explains why White Cherries can carry a noticeably resinous, fuel-oriented background despite its fruit-forward name.

Trop Cherry supplies the brighter half of the pedigree. Relentless Genetics created Tropicana Cherry—widely shortened to Trop Cherry—from Tropicana Cookies × Cherry Cookies F3. The breeder describes the selection as slightly sativa dominant, strongly colored, citrus-and-cherry flavored, and capable of producing an upbeat cerebral experience. Relentless also notes that its Trop Cherry breeding material reliably passes color and trichome development into offspring.

Combining those families creates a genetic tug-of-war that works in White Cherries’ favor. White Truffle contributes tighter structure, resin, earthy depth, and physical calm; Trop Cherry adds red-purple coloration, fruit, citrus brightness, and a more alert head effect. The cross itself has circulated among growers under closely related naming, including Frosty Cherry, before the White Cherries name became prominent in current commercial production. Because historical breeder documentation for the specific selection is limited, it is more accurate to preserve the confirmed White Truffle × Trop Cherry lineage than to invent a more detailed selection history.
Effects and Experience

White Cherries begins with a change in perspective rather than an immediate wave of heaviness. Mood tends to brighten, ordinary tasks can feel more interesting, and concentration may actually remain fairly organized at moderate amounts. The current commercial description emphasizes uplift and focus alongside relaxation, an effect profile that makes sense given the Trop Cherry parent. Rather than producing a sharp rush followed by a crash, the mental component feels comparatively smooth and sustained.

As time passes, White Truffle’s contribution becomes easier to recognize. Physical tension begins to soften and the high settles deeper into the body, yet the mind often remains present instead of drifting immediately toward sleep. That balance makes this hybrid suitable for music, conversation, hobbies, creative work, gaming, or simply unwinding without abandoning the rest of the evening. Larger amounts can still produce considerable impairment, but moderate consumption is less likely to feel overwhelmingly sedative than many modern dessert and gas hybrids.

Current Viking Cannabis flower demonstrates why potency should be judged from actual laboratory results rather than strain mythology. Retail batches have appeared around 18.3%, 18.8%, 19.5%, 20.1%, and 21% THC, with CBD generally below 0.1%. THC can temporarily affect memory, coordination, emotions, perception, and judgment, and larger doses may produce anxiety, fear, or panic in susceptible consumers.
Medical Benefits

The even progression from mental uplift into physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer cannabis that does not immediately produce couch-lock. Some people seek this type of hybrid when stress, discomfort, reduced appetite, or general physical tension interferes with their ability to relax while remaining mentally engaged. The comparatively moderate THC levels seen in current White Cherries batches may also make dose adjustment easier than with flower testing above 30%, although individual response to cannabis varies substantially.

No controlled clinical trial has established White Cherries itself as a treatment for pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical condition. Research involving cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly has found modest benefits for some chronic pain and multiple-sclerosis symptoms, while specific cannabinoid medications are approved for chemotherapy-related nausea and vomiting and for appetite and weight-loss problems associated with HIV/AIDS. Those findings concern cannabis or standardized cannabinoid medicines generally, not this particular marijuana cultivar.

The cultivar’s uplifting reputation should also not be interpreted as evidence that it treats stress or anxiety disorders. THC can produce relaxation at one dose and nervousness or panic at another. Anyone using weed for persistent symptoms should consider cannabinoid concentration, other medications, individual tolerance, method of consumption, and professional healthcare guidance rather than relying exclusively on a strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Cherry is immediately recognizable, but the fruit character is softer and richer than the sour-orange punch associated with many Trop Cherry crosses. Viking describes its selection as cherry pie forward with subtle cream, which captures the central flavor unusually well. The initial aroma can suggest ripe cherries or cherry filling, followed by cream and a faint pastry-like sweetness rather than bright artificial candy.

Breaking apart the flower reveals the White Truffle side. Earth, musky resin, fuel, and occasional Glue-like funk emerge underneath the sweeter surface. Grower observations of the original White Truffle × Trop Cherry cross have also described candy-fuel and Gorilla Glue-like undertones, demonstrating how strongly that savory parent can influence certain expressions. On the exhale, cherry sweetness frequently gives way to a drier combination of earth and gas.

No standardized terpene panel has been published for the cultivar across all Viking batches, making it inappropriate to declare one universal dominant terpene. Exact chemistry should come from the certificate of analysis for the particular flower. At strain level, cherry pie, cream, sweet fruit, earth, fuel, and musky resin provide a more defensible description than attaching unsupported terpene percentages.
Growing Information

White Cherries combines two parents with very different structural tendencies. White Truffle generally favors compact, resin-heavy flower formation, while Trop Cherry can introduce more stretch, color, and an open hybrid structure. Growers should therefore expect meaningful phenotype variation. Some plants may remain relatively compact and Truffle dominant; others can carry more of Trop Cherry’s vertical growth and brighter pigmentation.

Approximately eight to nine weeks of flowering is a practical indoor range. Related Trop Cherry breeding material from Relentless commonly finishes around nine weeks or less, while documented growers of the White Truffle × Trop Cherry cross have harvested around day 63. Topping or low-stress training can help distribute branches across the canopy, but aggressive training late in vegetative growth is unnecessary if the plant already develops strong lateral structure.

Yield appears more focused on quality than exceptional bulk. Grower documentation of the cross describes moderate production but particularly impressive resin and aroma, a pattern consistent with Trop Cherry-influenced boutique hybrids. Dense trichome coverage makes late-flower humidity control important, while adequate airflow helps protect the interior of the buds. Outdoors, plants following an eight-to-nine-week flowering pattern will generally finish around late September into early October in suitable northern climates, although latitude and seasonal weather determine the actual harvest date.
FAQ
What are the genetics of White Cherries?

White Cherries is White Truffle × Trop Cherry. White Truffle comes from the Gorilla Butter family associated with Fresh Coast Seed Company, while Trop Cherry was created by Relentless Genetics from Tropicana Cookies × Cherry Cookies F3.
Who bred White Cherries?

The underlying White Truffle × Trop Cherry cross has been attributed to Grow More Fire Genetics, while the currently prominent White Cherries commercial selection is cultivated and marketed by Viking Cannabis in Washington.
Is White Cherries indica or sativa?
It is best described as a balanced hybrid. Trop Cherry contributes brighter cerebral qualities, while White Truffle supplies greater physical relaxation and earthy resin character.
How strong is White Cherries?

Current Viking Cannabis flower commonly tests around 18–21% THC, with CBD usually well below 0.1%. Individual harvests vary, so the laboratory result on the specific product provides the most accurate potency figure.
What does White Cherries taste like?

The flavor centers on cherry pie and sweet cherry with subtle cream, followed by earth, musky resin, and light fuel. The fruitier qualities come largely from Trop Cherry, while White Truffle adds the darker savory foundation.
Final Thoughts on White Cherries

White Cherries succeeds because its parents contribute nearly opposite personalities. Trop Cherry brings brilliant fruit, citrus, color, and an alert cerebral quality; White Truffle answers with pale resin, earth, fuel, dense flowers, and a calmer physical foundation. The finished weed lands between them rather than allowing one side to erase the other. Cherry pie and cream lead the flavor, but enough Truffle funk survives underneath to keep the cultivar from becoming another straightforward fruit strain.

Its current potency also makes White Cherries interesting in a market increasingly obsessed with inflated THC numbers. Commercial examples around the high teens to low 20% range can still deliver a clearly intoxicating experience while putting more emphasis on flavor, focus, balance, and resin quality. For consumers looking for modern boutique cannabis that remains functional at moderate doses—and growers interested in combining Trop Cherry color with White Truffle frost—White Cherries offers a distinctive meeting point between two of the more recognizable genetic families of contemporary marijuana.
